newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-LIVERPOOL GAMBLE ON THREE STRIKERS TO BEAT PSG.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-LIVERPOOL GAMBLE ON THREE STRIKERS TO BEAT PSG.

text.p: Liverpool will play with a three-man attack for the first time this season when they attempt to overcome a three goal deficit in their European Cup Winners' Cup semifinal against holders Paris St Germain at Anfield on Thursday.

Coach Roy Evans is expected to start wth Robbie Fowler, Stan Collymore and Patrick Berger in an attacking opening gambit which he hopes will help Liverpool turn what looks like certain defeat into an unlikely success.
And he is also expected to keep faith with goalkeeper David James whose mistakes in recent weeks have cost Liverpool vital goals and points.

James, whose lack of form has also cost him his place in the England squad less than a month after making his debut, said he will come through his current problems and is keen not to be dropped for the match.

"When everyone points out your mistakes in the smallest detail it can be very difficult," he said. "And I mean everyone. It is not nice going to the supermarket and the woman at the till thinking: 'Dodgy keeper'
"But I have been through this before at the start of my career at Liverpool and although I wanted to be dropped then, I don't now."
Liverpool where well beaten 3-0 in Paris and gave what many people feel was not only their worst performance of the season, but also their worst in Europe in almost 30 years.
Evans said he is also likely to start with a flat back four for the first time this season.

"Anything is possible. We cannot sit back and be too sensible. The only good thing that can come out of the way we played in Paris is that we cannot play as badly again. Of course we've got a mountain to climb, but we will not go out without a very determined effort to pull something out of the tie."

Liverpool will be without suspended defender Steve Harkness and the ineligible Bjorn Tore Kvarme so defenders Phil Babb, Neil Ruddock, Rob Jones and Dominic Matteo all come into contention for a place in the starting line-up.
Despite their first leg lead, PSG remain cautious ahead of their fifth semifinal of an European Cup competition in consecutive years.
"It will be a different story (from the first match) this time," predicted defender Bruno Ngotty. "Liverpool will be playing to save their season and they will put us under a lot of pressure."
Manager Ricardo said he thought Liverpool would change their tactics.
"I expect them to be much more aggressive than in the first leg," he said. "That might create some space for us to counter-attack."
Brazilian Rai said PSG, now too far behind Monaco to win the league title, badly needed a win to restore their confidence and fuel their fight for a place in next season's Champions' League.

"A win would do our confidence a lot of good and would help us fight for that second place (in the French league)," he said. "We are always under a lot of pressure because people expect us to do well," he said. "But I like that and I'm used to it. It's even worse in Brazil."

Liverpool (from) - David James, Rob Jones, Dominic Matteo, Mark Wright, Neil Ruddock, Jason McAteer, John Barnes, Michael Thomas, Jamie Redknapp, Robbie Fowler, Patrick Berger, Steve McManaman, Stan Collymore.
PSG (probable) - Bernard Lama, Laurent Fournier, Bruno Ngotty, Paul Le Guen, Jimmy Algerino, Vincent Guerin, Benoit Cauet, Jerome Leroy, Rai, Leonardo, Patrice Loko.
